'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2021 Israel–Palestine crisis]]
**Further [[airstrike]]s by the [[Israel Defense Forces|IDF]] are conducted at sites north of [[Beit Lahia]] and in [[Gaza City]] belonging to armed [[militia]] groups, as well as a civil administration building in [[Jabalia]] and an agriculture field near [[Khan Yunis]]. [[Hamas]] media outlet [[Al-Aqsa TV]] says Hamas downed an [[Israel]]i [[Unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]]. No casualties are reported. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/17/israeli-air-raids-target-gaza-strip-for-second-time-since-truce (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on tourism]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on The Walt Disney Company]]
**[[Disneyland Paris]], Europe's most visited [[amusement park]], reopens for the second time with enhanced health and safety measures after being closed for eight months due to the second wave of the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. It is the first time that all [[Disney Parks, Experiences and Products|Disney-owned and licensed theme parks]] have been open since January 2020. [https://www.francebleu.fr/infos/culture-loisirs/disneyland-paris-rouvre-ce-jeudi-apres-sept-mois-de-fermeture-et-le-masque-est-obligatoire-1623877225 (France Bleu)] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/travel/experience/america/theme-parks/2021/06/17/disney-parks-worldwide-disneyland-paris-reopening-marks-milestone/7727776002/ (''USA Today'')]
*[[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Joe Biden]] signs a law that would make [[Juneteenth]] a federal holiday, thereby making it the first federal holiday since the 1983 establishment of [[Martin Luther King Jr. Day]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/biden-juneteenth-holiday-bill-2021-06-17/ (CBS News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Afghanistan]]
****[[COVID-19 lockdowns]], [[Afghanistan–United States relations]]
*****The [[Embassy of the United States, Kabul|U.S. Embassy]] in [[Kabul]] orders a lockdown on the building amid a rise of cases. [https://www.armytimes.com/news/pentagon-congress/2021/06/17/us-locks-down-embassy-in-afghanistan-amid-covid-19-surge/ (''Army Times'')]
****[[Afghanistan]] reports a record 515 new cases and 101 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://m.timesofindia.com/world/south-asia/covid-19-out-of-control-in-afghanistan-as-cases-up-2400-in-a-month/amp_articleshow/83604176.cms (''The Times of India'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Madhya Pradesh]]
*****[[Madhya Pradesh]] detects their first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]] in [[Bhopal]]. [https://www.indiatoday.in/coronavirus-outbreak/story/madhya-pradesh-records-first-covid-19-patient-with-delta-plus-variant-1816165-2021-06-17 (India Today)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Japan]]ese [[Prime Minister of Japan|Prime Minister]] [[Yoshihide Suga]] announces that the [[state of emergency]] will be lifted in nine [[Prefectures of Japan|prefecture]]s on June 21. However, the [[Government of Japan|government]] will maintain its quasi-emergency measures in seven prefectures, including [[Tokyo]] and [[Osaka Prefecture|Osaka]]. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/06/17/national/soe-lifting-nine-prefectures/ (''The Japan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kyrgyzstan]]
****[[Kyrgyzstan]] receives a shipment of 80,000 doses of the [[Russia]]n [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] [[COVID-19 vaccine]]. [https://24.kg/english/198047_80000_doses_of_Russian_Sputnik_V_vaccine_delivered_to_Kyrgyzstan/ (24.kg)]
****Kyrgyzstan reports a record of 787 new cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours. [http://en.kabar.kg/news/kyrgyzstan-sets-covid-19-daily-case-record-since-beginning-of-year/ (Kabar)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Sri Lanka]]
****[[Sri Lanka]] reports its first community case of the highly transmissible [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] [[Delta variant]] in five patients. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/international/coronavirus-sri-lanka-reports-delta-variant-amid-a-daunting-third-wave/article34843288.ece (''The Hindu'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] reports a record of 515 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 12,014. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/covid-19-vietnam-record-515-new-cases-15034424 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Portugal|Portuguese]] [[Government of Portugal|authorities]] announce that travel in and out of the [[Lisbon metropolitan area]] will be banned on weekends from Friday at 3:00 p.m. until Monday at 6:00 a.m. amid an increase in the number of [[COVID-19]] cases. [https://abcnews.go.com/Health/wireStory/lisbon-ringed-off-weekends-portugal-fights-virus-surge-78337824 (ABC News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Ukraine]]
****[[Ukraine]] reports a new single-day record of 76,538 doses of the [[COVID-19 vaccine]] administered. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/ukraine-sets-domestic-record-daily-covid-19-vaccinations-2021-06-17/ (Reuters)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
****The [[Australia]]n [[Australian Government|federal government]] restricts the usage of the [[Oxford–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine|Oxford–AstraZeneca]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] to people over the age of 60 following a new recommendation from the [[Australian Technical Advisory Group on Immunisation]]. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-06-17/atagi-to-change-astrazeneca-age-rules-covid-vaccine/100222464 (ABC Australia)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] reports a record 121 cases of [[COVID-19]] in the past 24 hours, as new clusters are discovered, thereby bringing the national total to 1,443. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/444915/fiji-records-121-new-covid-19-cases (RNZ)] [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2021-06/17/c_1310012521.htm (Xinhuanet)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]]
****[[Illinois]] becomes the first state in [[Midwestern United States|the Midwest]] to vaccinate 70% of adults. [https://www.wqad.com/article/news/health/coronavirus/illinois-vaccination-prize-lottery/526-9e4fdf73-5c9b-471b-9dff-cc37a5d432ac (WQAD-TV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Zambia]]
***[[Zambia]]n [[Government of Zambia|authorities]] order the closure of schools for the next 21 days and also suspend election campaigns for the [[2021 Zambian general election|general election in August]] after reporting the highest number of deaths due to COVID-19 in one day. At the same time, the authorities restrict activities in religious sites to meetings only twice a week and for only one hour per day. [https://www.europapress.es/internacional/noticia-zambia-cierra-colegios-suspende-actos-campana-electoral-repunte-casos-coronavirus-20210617123347.html (Europa Press)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Tigray War]]
**The [[African Union]] (AU) launches an official commission to investigate allegations of [[human rights in Ethiopia|human rights]] abuses committed in [[Ethiopia]]'s [[Tigray Region]]. The Ethiopian Foreign Ministry rejects the commission as "misguided" and without legal basis, saying that a joint probe by the AU and Ethiopia should be used instead. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/17/african-union-launches-probe-alleged-rights-abuses-tigray (Al Jazeera)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**Police in [[Hong Kong]] arrest five executives of the ''[[Apple Daily]]'' newspaper as the newspaper warns that press freedom in the city is "hanging by a thread". It is the latest raid on the Beijing-critical newspaper which has already seen its chief [[Jimmy Lai]] convicted under various charges, including unlawful assembly, and who currently faces a national security law case along with 46 other activists. [https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20210617-hong-kong-police-arrest-five-at-pro-democracy-newspaper-apple-daily (France 24)]
*[[Shooting of Eyad al-Hallaq]]
**An Israeli police officer is charged with "reckless [[homicide]]" for killing an [[autistic]] [[Palestinians|Palestinian]] adult in [[Jerusalem]]'s [[Old City (Jerusalem)|Old City]] in May 2020. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210617-israeli-officer-charged-with-killing-autistic-palestinian (France 24)]
*[[St. Louis gun-toting controversy]]
**Pro-gun activists Mark and Patricia McCloskey plead guilty to misdemeanor charges relating to an incident last year where they brandished weapons at [[Black Lives Matter]] protesters during a [[George Floyd protest]] in [[St. Louis]], [[Missouri]], United States. They also agree to give up their guns and pay [[United States dollar|US$]]2,750 in total fines. [https://www.dw.com/en/couple-who-pointed-guns-at-blm-protesters-plead-guilty/a-57945667 (DW)]
*One person is killed, four are shot and eight are otherwise injured in eight [[drive-by shooting]]s in the [[West Valley (Phoenix metropolitan area)|West Valley]] area near [[Phoenix, Arizona]], United States. A male suspect is taken into custody. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/least-9-injured-series-drive-shootings-arizona-suspect-custody-n1271259 (NBC News)]
*A person is killed when a gunman opens fire on the offices of pro-[[Kurds in Turkey|Kurdish]] opposition party [[Peoples' Democratic Party (Turkey)|People's Democratic Party]] (HDP) in [[İzmir]], [[İzmir Province]], [[Turkey]]. The gunman also attempted to [[arson|set fire]] to the office building. HDP [[Grand National Assembly of Turkey|MP]] from İzmir [[Serpil Kemalbay]] blames the current government for the attack, saying that officials were inciting violence against the party and its supporters. [https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/turkey-kurdish-hdp-gunman-kills-employee-attack-izmir (''Middle East Eye'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*''[[California v. Texas]]'', [[Efforts to repeal the Affordable Care Act]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United States|United States Supreme Court]], in a 7–2 decision, dismisses a challenge to the [[Affordable Care Act]] brought before the court by [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]]-led states and the former [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]]. The Court stated that the challengers did not specify an injury caused by the ACA to establish standing. [https://www.law.cornell.edu/supremecourt/text/19-840 (LII)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-57516488 (BBC News)]
*[[Elections in the United Kingdom]], [[2021 Chesham and Amersham by-election]]
**The [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] gains the [[Chesham and Amersham (UK Parliament constituency)|Chesham and Amersham]] seat in a shock defeat to the ruling [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] government. The Conservatives suffers a swing of 25.2% away from them in a by-election billed as a sign of further [[Political realignment|realignment]] in British politics. This is the first time that a non-Conservative MP represents the constituency. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2021/jun/18/lib-dems-win-chesham-and-amersham-byelection-in-stunning-upset (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Repeal of the 2002 AUMF]]
**The [[United States House of Representatives]] votes 268–161 to repeal the [[Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq Resolution of 2002]], a resolution that granted U.S. presidents the authority to engage in [[Iraq War|war]] with [[Iraq]]. The bill will now head to the [[United States Senate]]. [https://www.npr.org/2021/06/17/1007363054/congress-is-poised-to-take-back-some-of-its-war-powers-from-the-president (NPR)]
*The U.S. Supreme Court rejects a lawsuit brought by six African men against American food corporation [[Cargill]] and the American division of [[Nestlé]] for their [[Child labour in cocoa production|use of child slavery]] in [[cocoa bean]] production in a 8–1 decision, saying that because the abuses took place outside the country, the Court did not have jurisdiction on the matter. [https://www.reuters.com/business/us-supreme-court-rules-nestle-cargill-over-slavery-lawsuit-2021-06-17/ (Reuters)]
*Former Ivorian President [[Laurent Gbagbo]] returns to [[Abidjan]], [[Ivory Coast]], for the first time in nearly 10 years, after the [[International Criminal Court]] upheld his acquittal for his role in the [[2010–2011 Ivorian crisis|violence committed in the aftermath]] of the [[2010 Ivorian presidential election|2010 presidential elections]] earlier this year. The government of current president [[Alassane Ouattara]] supported his return as necessary for reconciliation, but did not comment if he will be imprisoned for misappropriating funds from a regional bank, for which he was sentenced to 20 years in prison in November 2019. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/6/17/former-president-laurent-gbagbo-returns-to-ivory-coast (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Member of Parliament (Canada)|Canada MPs]] in the [[House of Commons of Canada|House of Commons]] votes to censure [[Minister of National Defence (Canada)|Defense Minister]] [[Harjit Sajjan]] over his handling of [[Sexual assault in the Canadian Forces|sexual misconduct]] in the [[Canadian Armed Forces]]. [https://globalnews.ca/news/7957711/canadian-forces-sexual-misconduct-harjit-sajjan-censure/ (Global News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[China]] launches the [[Shenzhou 12]] spacecraft carrying three [[astronaut]]s on the first flight to the [[Tianhe core module]]. [https://elpais.com/ciencia/2021-06-17/china-lanza-con-exito-una-mision-tripulada-a-su-estacion-espacial.html (''El País'')]
*French scientists announce in a ''[[Current Biology]]'' paper that [[coelacanth]]s are capable of living up to 100 years, contrary to the long-held belief that they only live up to 20 years. [https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/jun/18/mysterious-coelacanth-fish-can-live-for-100-years-study (''The Guardian'')]
